title: GST Return Filing in 2026: How to File Online and Check Due Dates
summary: Learn how to file GST returns in 2026 with updated rules, dates, steps, ITC changes, and penalties explained.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Filing GST returns on time is important for every business as missing a deadline can lead to penalties and other consequences. The GST portal generally bars specified returns and statements after 3 years from their due date.


With the GST Council rolling out reforms such as more stringent input tax credit eligibility norms, real-time ledger validations, and mandatory bank detail updates, businesses must be proactive in filing their GST returns on time. Monthly filers generally must meet the 11th and 20th deadlines. Similarly, quarterly filers face state-based staggered schedules. Businesses further need to match purchases with GSTR-2B and check eligibility before claiming ITC.


This guide breaks down everything you need to know to file GST returns in 2026 accurately and on time.


### TL;DR


- File GSTR-1 to report outward supplies. Use GSTR-3B to report your GST liability, claim eligible input tax credit and pay any tax due.
- Monthly GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are generally due on the 11th and 20th of the following month, respectively. QRMP filers follow quarterly deadlines.
- If you have no reportable activity, check whether you qualify to file a nil return. Select the applicable period on the GST portal’s Returns Dashboard.


##


What Is GST Return Filing?


Every tax-registered business is supposed to file its[GST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-gst-goods-and-service-tax/) return in India, with statements of sales, purchases, tax paid, and input tax credits. Filing of these returns declares your tax liability to the tax authorities. There are different types of GST returns.


Every registered taxable person must file their returns, but this depends on the scale and nature of the business. For regular taxpayers with turnover above ₹5 crore, they must do two kinds of monthly returns: GSTR-1, which details sales outwards, and GSTR-3B, which summarizes sales, credit, and tax paid. An annual return GSTR-9 completes the yearly cycle, where applicable.


Smaller businesses with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore can opt for the QRMP (Quarterly Return Monthly Payment) scheme if eligible, filing GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B quarterly instead of monthly. Composition dealers under the simplified composition scheme file quarterly statement CMP-08 and annual return GSTR-4. Specialized returns exist for e-commerce operators,[TDS](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gstr-7-due-date-late-fees-how-to-file/) /TCS deductors, and non-resident taxpayers, but most businesses work primarily with GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, and GSTR-9.


Filing remains mandatory for all GST-registered entities. Non-filing triggers GSTR-3B late fees of ₹50 per day (₹25 CGST + ₹25[SGST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-sgst/) ) for regular returns, subject to the applicable cap, plus 18% interest per annum on overdue tax. The system enforces sequential filing. You generally cannot file December’s return if November remains pending, creating cascading blocks that multiply penalties.


##


GST Return Filing Rules in 2026


From FY 2025–26 onwards, various rules and portal validations have affected GST filing.


### Three-Year Limit for Filing Older GST Returns


The GST portal now prevents filing specified GST returns and statements more than three years past their due dates. Returns pending beyond this window generally become unavailable for filing. One missed return from 2021 cannot be filed in 2026. The regime promotes compliance and cuts compliance arrears that have long existed.


### Late Fees for Annual Returns


Filing the annual return late can trigger late fees based on your turnover slab. If GSTR-9C is required, late fees can continue until both GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C are filed. The December 31 annual return deadline demands strict adherence.


### ITC and Ledger Verification


The GSTN portal checks ledger conditions during GSTR-3B submission. You should review unpaid reverse charge liabilities and any negative statement balances before filing. Input tax credit claims need to be reconciled against your auto-generated GSTR-2B statement where applicable. Check the other legal conditions before claiming ITC.


### Mandatory Bank Account Details


Failing to furnish valid bank account details in your GST profile can trigger automatic registration suspension. A suspended GSTIN can restrict return filing and e-way bill generation. The rule combats fake registrations and improves transparency, requiring businesses to maintain updated profile information.


### Turnover Thresholds


Recalculate your Aggregate Annual Turnover and check if it passes your applicable[registration threshold](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-registration-online-process-documents/) . The general thresholds are ₹20 lakh for services and up to ₹40 lakh for eligible suppliers of goods, with exceptions. Composition scheme businesses exceeding the applicable turnover limit must shift to the regular GST regime. Non-registration when required invites penalties.


##


GST 2.0 Tax Slabs and Rate Changes


The GST Council’s 56th meeting in late 2025 introduced major slab simplification carried into 2026. The complex multi-tier structure (5%, 12%, 18%, 28% plus special rates) has shifted towards two main slabs under GST 2.0.


**Category** **Previous GST rate examples** **Revised GST rate examples**


Main GST slabs 5%, 12%, 18% and 28% 5% (merit rate) and 18% (standard rate)


Select luxury and demerit goods 28% plus cess in certain cases 40% for specified goods, including certain high-end vehicles and beverages


Essentials such as pre-packaged and labelled paneer and UHT milk 5% Nil for specified items


Selected household items such as shampoo and toothpaste 18% 5%


Selected appliances such as air conditioners and dishwashers 28% 18%


Effective September 22, 2025, most revised rates took effect, with two primary slabs: 5% and 18%. The old 12% and 28% rates were largely eliminated. A special 40% rate applies to select “demerit” goods such as certain high-sugar beverages and luxury vehicles. The zero percent category continues for essential items.


Most goods and services now fall under either 5% (merit rate) or 18% (standard rate). Common household and food items previously taxed at 12% or 18% have been reduced to 5% in many cases. The rationalization simplifies tax calculations.


Businesses must update accounting systems and price labels to reflect new rates. GST returns must apply the correct rates for all sales from the effective date. Incorrect rate application leads to underpayment or overpayment in GSTR-3B, creating compliance issues.


Specific sectors continue seeing adjustments. Tobacco products saw additional changes effective February 1, 2026, under separate notifications. Businesses in these categories should monitor GST Council notifications closely.


For most businesses, GST rates in 2026 are more streamlined. Verify your product/service[HSN codes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/hsn-sac-code-gst/) against the[latest rate list](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/new-gst-rates/) to ensure accurate charging and reporting.


##


How to File GST Return Online


Online GST return filings for 2026 are a systematic process that will help in achieving compliance and easy credit flow. The following are the steps that will facilitate proper GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B filing and cover the requirements for other filers.


### Step 1. Prepare the Required Documents


Before logging in, gather:


- Sales invoices categorized into B2B, large B2C (interstate invoices above ₹1 lakh), and export invoices
- Credit or debit notes issued during the period
- Purchase invoices for claiming Input Tax Credit
- Sales summaries organized by GST rate and HSN code
- GSTIN and login credentials ready


### Step 2. Log In to the GST Portal


- Visit gst.gov.in and enter your[GST portal username and password](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-login-password-portal-guide/)
- Navigate to Services → Returns → Returns Dashboard
- Select the financial year and tax period (month or quarter) for filing
- Verify applicable return forms displayed for your taxpayer category


### Step 3. File GSTR-1 for Outward Supplies


- Click “Prepare Online” under GSTR-1 for the selected period
- Enter B2B sales with buyer GSTIN and complete invoice details
- Add B2C large invoices, exports, and credit/debit notes in respective sections
- Ensure correct invoice numbers, dates,[customer GSTINs](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-verification/) , taxable values, and GST rates
- Save work section-wise and validate the summary for errors
- Submit GSTR-1 using DSC (Digital Signature Certificate) or EVC (Electronic Verification Code)


*Note: E-invoicing users verify auto-populated sales details before submission*


### Step 4. File GSTR-3B and Pay GST


- Select GSTR-3B and click “Prepare Online”
- Review auto-filled figures from GSTR-1 in outward supplies section
- Enter total taxable value and GST for all outward supplies
- Input eligible ITC on imports and domestic purchases after reconciling with GSTR-2B and your records
- Verify system-calculated net tax payable after ITC offset
- Offset liability using available ITC credits from electronic credit ledger
- Pay any remaining balance through electronic cash ledger
- Submit GSTR-3B with DSC or EVC by the applicable due date to avoid 18% interest and late fees


### Step 5. Check QRMP and Composition Filing Requirements


**For QRMP Taxpayers (Quarterly Filers)**


- File GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B quarterly instead of monthly
- Optionally upload B2B invoices via Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) by the 13th in the first two months
- Complete quarterly GSTR-1 by the 13th of the month following quarter-end
- File quarterly GSTR-3B by the 22nd or 24th (based on state grouping)


**For Composition Taxpayers**


- File simplified quarterly CMP-08 by the 18th of the month after each quarter
- Enter total quarterly sales and self-assessed tax amount
- Pay computed tax liability through the portal
- File annual GSTR-4 by 30 June following the financial year, summarizing yearly turnover and taxes paid


### Step 6. File GSTR-9 Where Applicable


- Access GSTR-9 after financial year-end (due by 31 December following the financial year, where filing is required)


Registered persons with aggregate turnover up to ₹2 crore are exempt from filing GSTR-9 for the relevant financial year under Notification No. 15/2025–Central Tax, effective from FY 2024–25 onwards.


- Download system-computed summary with pre-filled data from monthly returns
- Cross-verify pre-filled figures against your books of accounts
- Provide details of total sales, purchases, tax paid, and claimed credits for the year
- Reconcile discrepancies between monthly filings and annual figures
- Prepare the self-certified GSTR-9C reconciliation statement if aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore
- If using the offline tool, generate a JSON file and upload it to the portal
- Submit GSTR-9 using the applicable filing method. The return cannot be revised once filed, so verify thoroughly


##


How to Amend GSTR-1 Using GSTR-1A Before Filing GSTR-3B


Once you file GSTR-1, it cannot be directly revised. However, the GST system allows you to correct errors using GSTR-1A, an amendment form introduced in July 2024. This is critical because incorrect GSTR-1 data flows into your GSTR-3B and can affect the buyer’s ITC (Input Tax Credit) records.


### What Is GSTR-1A?


GSTR-1A is an optional amendment form that allows you to correct or add invoice details from the current tax period’s GSTR-1. It must be filed before you submit your GSTR-3B for that tax period. Once GSTR-3B is filed, GSTR-1A is no longer available for that period.


**Common GSTR-1A Scenarios**


**Scenario 1:** You filed GSTR-1 on the 11th but missed some invoices. On the 15th, you realize 5 invoices weren’t uploaded. File GSTR-1A before filing GSTR-3B for the same period to add these missing invoices.


**Scenario 2:** Your GSTR-1 shows the wrong invoice amount (₹10,000 instead of ₹15,000). File GSTR-1A to correct this before GSTR-3B, so the corrected value can flow to the buyer’s GSTR-2B in the next cycle.


**Scenario 3:** You entered the wrong buyer GSTIN. Correct the recipient GSTIN through the applicable amendment in a later GSTR-1 or IFF period. GSTR-1A does not allow edits to the recipient GSTIN.


**Key Rules for GSTR-1A**


- Must be filed before GSTR-3B submission for that period.
- Can only amend current period’s GSTR-1 (not past months).
- Cannot be amended after filing (no GSTR-1A to GSTR-1A amendments).
- Corrected data flows into GSTR-3B immediately and to your buyer’s GSTR-2B in the next generation cycle.


##


How to File a Nil GST Return


A nil return is a GST filing where you have no details to report for that form in the relevant tax period. Many small business owners assume they don’t need to file if they have no business activity. This is incorrect and can lead to late fees.


### When Is Nil GST Return Filing Mandatory?


Regular taxpayers must file their applicable returns each month or quarter, even if there were zero sales or purchases. For nil GSTR-3B, check that you have no outward or inward supplies, ITC to claim, or tax liability to report. Filing a nil return is a legal requirement for taxpayers who must file a return for that period. Late fees may apply after the applicable due date.


### Nil GST Return Late Fees vs Regular Returns


While nil return late fees are lower than regular returns, they still apply and accumulate daily.


- Regular GSTR-3B (with tax liability). ₹50/day late fee (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST), capped at ₹2,000-₹10,000 depending on turnover
- Nil GSTR-3B. ₹20/day late fee (₹10 CGST + ₹10 SGST), capped at ₹500


If you file a nil GSTR-3B 10 days late, you owe ₹200 in late fees (₹20 × 10 days). While lower than regular return penalties, this still applies even though you had no tax liability.


### How to File a Nil GST Return Online or by SMS


To[file nil GSTR-3B online](https://tutorial.gst.gov.in/userguide/returns/GSTR3B_-_File_Nil_Return.htm) , log in to the GST portal, open **Services → Returns → Returns Dashboard** , select your tax period, and choose **Prepare Online** under GSTR-3B. Select **Yes** for the nil return option if eligible, preview the draft, and file using DSC or EVC. For nil GSTR-1, open the GSTR-1 tile for the same period and use its nil filing option if eligible.


The GST system provides an easy SMS facility for filing nil GSTR-3B returns. If you meet the nil filing conditions for the tax period, you can file via SMS directly without logging into the portal, using the authorised signatory’s registered mobile number. Eligible filers can also submit nil GSTR-1 by SMS.


##


GST Return Filing Due Dates in 2026


### GST Filing Deadlines at a Glance


GST filing has very strict deadlines, and any delay leads to late fees or interest on overdue tax. The main GST filing deadlines to remain GST-compliant are listed below. Check the GST portal for any notified extensions.


**Filing type** **Form** **Standard due date**


Monthly GSTR-1 11th of the following month


Monthly GSTR-3B 20th of the following month


QRMP GSTR-1 13th of the month after the quarter ends


QRMP GSTR-3B 22nd or 24th of the month after the quarter ends, depending on the[principal place of business](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-state-code-list/)


QRMP PMT-06 25th of the following month for the first two months of the quarter, where payment is due


Composition CMP-08 18th of the month after the quarter ends


Composition GSTR-4 30 June following the financial year


Annual GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C, where applicable 31 December following the financial year


**Monthly filers** : GSTR-1 to be filed for the last month’s sale is to be submitted by the 11th of every month. GSTR-3B along with payment is to be submitted by the 20th of every month. Eligible taxpayers with turnover of ₹5 crore or less may also file monthly if they do not opt for QRMP.


**Quarterly filers under the QRMP scheme** : Optional IFF is available for furnishing eligible invoices for the first two months of a quarter, by the 13th of the following month in each case. Quarterly GSTR-1 is generally due on the 13th of the month following the quarter. For Apr to Jun Quarter 2026, the standard due date for filing Q1 GSTR-1 was July 13. States have different filing dates for GSTR-3B, filed on the 22nd or 24th of the month following the quarter. Payments through PMT-06 for the first two months, where due, are payable by the 25th of the following month.


**Composition dealers** : File CMP-08 on or before the 18th day of the month following each quarter. Accordingly, for the Apr-Jun quarter, the CMP-08 is required to be filed by July 18. GSTR-4 is required to be filed by 30 June following the financial year.


**Annual returns:** GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C, where applicable, are to be submitted by December 31 of the succeeding fiscal year. Extensions might be allowed, but prepare for the December 31 deadline. Late filing triggers per-day late fees capped by turnover category.


##


GST Late Fees: Calculation and Examples


Late fees are not optional. They are automatically calculated and charged by the portal when you file after the due date. Understanding how they’re calculated helps you plan cash flow and avoid surprises.


### GSTR-3B Late Fee Formula and Rates


For GSTR-3B, the late fee is generally ₹50 per day (for regular returns with tax liability) or ₹20 per day (for nil returns with zero tax), subject to the applicable cap or waiver.


The fee is divided equally between ₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST for regular returns or ₹10 CGST + ₹10 SGST for nil returns.


### Worked Examples of Late Fee Calculation


#### Example 1. Regular Return Filed Late


You file GSTR-3B for January on February 23rd (3 days after the 20th due date). Days delayed = 3. Late fee = ₹50 × 3 = ₹150 (₹75 CGST + ₹75 SGST). You must pay this ₹150 in cash via the electronic cash ledger. You cannot use your ITC to pay late fees.


#### Example 2. Nil Return Filed Late


You file a nil GSTR-3B for January on February 28th (8 days late). Days delayed = 8. Late fee = ₹20 × 8 = ₹160 (₹80 CGST + ₹80 SGST). Even though you had zero tax, you still owe this late fee.


#### Example 3. Interest on Delayed Tax Payment


You owe ₹10,000 in GST for January, due February 20. You pay on March 5 (13 days late). Assuming no eligible cash-ledger balance reduces the tax base, the interest calculation is (₹10,000 × 18% × 13 days) ÷ 365 = ₹64. If you also file late, the late fee is charged separately.


#### Key Points About Late Fees


Late fees apply even for nil returns. The maximum combined GSTR-3B late fees for returns with tax liability vary by turnover: ₹2,000 (≤₹1.5 Cr) | ₹5,000 (₹1.5-5 Cr) | ₹10,000 (>₹5 Cr). Late fees must be paid through the electronic cash ledger. The portal auto-calculates these and blocks filing until you pay. Interest at 18% p.a. applies separately for late payment of tax (not just late filing).


##


GST Compliance Checks for FY 2026–27


From 1 April 2026, the start of FY 2026–27, you will need to be aware of compliance requirements related to GST filing. You should be prepared to avoid disruption and penalties.


### E-Invoicing Thresholds and Reporting Time


E-invoicing generally applies to notified taxpayers with aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore in any applicable preceding financial year. Businesses with aggregate annual turnover of ₹10 crore or more must[report applicable e-invoices](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-rules-regulations/) within 30 days of the document date.


### Invoice and Credit Note Numbering for the New Financial Year


Starting April 1, check that your document numbers are unique for the financial year for invoices, debit notes, and credit notes. A new series can help distinguish documents by financial year. For example: If your March 2026 invoices were numbered up to INV-12345, you could start a fresh series from 1 April, such as INV/26-27/001. Rule 46 allows consecutive numbering that is unique to the financial year.


### Electronic Credit Reversal and Reclaimed Statement (ECRS)


The GST portal uses ECRS to monitor all ITC reversals and subsequent reclaims. A negative closing balance or an excess reclaim can trigger portal validations when filing GSTR-3B. Therefore, it is imperative that you continually check your ledger balance and resolve any negative positions as soon as possible.


### Credit Note Rejection Tracking


Once you submit a credit note via GSTR-1, your buyer can either accept or reject it. If your buyer rejects a credit note in the Invoice Management System (IMS), check the effect on your output tax liability in GSTR-3B. Immediately communicate with buyers whenever credit notes are issued to minimize rejections.


##


Best Practices for GST Compliance in 2026


Due to stricter rules, it is advisable that you follow a few best practices and be disciplined towards ensuring smooth compliance and avoiding penalties. Below are some necessary practices to ensure seamless GST filing in 2026:


### File Returns Timely and Sequentially


Ensure you file your Returns at the same time every month so that your returns do not get blocked due to non-filing of prior periods. With the introduction of the 3 year restriction on filing of older returns, timely filing of each month’s return is now more important than ever. Covered returns generally become unavailable for filing after three years from their due date. Continuous filing will also help to avoid cascading blocking of later Returns that can lead to exponential growth of late fees across many different periods. Timely filing of Returns allows you to maintain continuous operation of your business.


### Reconcile Monthly to Avoid ITC Issues


Use GSTR-2B monthly to reconcile purchases and verify all expected credits appear correctly. Check GSTR-2B and the other eligibility conditions before claiming ITC to avoid mismatches and subsequent reversal notices. Missing credits require immediate supplier follow-up rather than risky claims that may be disallowed. Reconcile sales with GSTR-1 to catch errors early, allowing amendments in subsequent returns.


### Use Correct HSN Codes and Tax Rates


For HSN reporting, use official GST rate lists provided by government websites when creating invoices to ensure correct application of tax rates. Update point of sale systems and accounting software to include correct GST rates effective from FY 2026 as soon as they are released. Incorrect classification of goods/services will cause short payment issues that will be detected upon audit, subjecting you to penalties and interest.


### Avoid Common Filing Errors


Before submitting returns, check invoice numbers, GSTIN accuracy & mandatory field completion. Although errors discovered post submission can be amended in the next return period via amendment mechanism in GST portal; early correction eliminates possibility of annual return reconciliation issues and potential discrepancies in GSTR-9.


### Leverage E-Invoicing and Technology


E-Invoicing (required for businesses with turnover over ₹5 crore) auto populates data into GSTR-1 reducing manual data entry & errors. Gst accounting software auto imports data, matches credits and generates returns for review. Using technology can reduce human error and speed up return preparation. Spending money on tools for compliance is a wise investment considering potential penalties, interest and costs associated with audits.


### Keep Business Information Updated


Regularly update your company’s GST profile details such as primary business address, contact info & bank accounts. Updating changes in location or additional locations requires you to file amendments promptly via GST portal. Keeping your profile current can help avoid interruptions to operations and return filing. Keeping your contact information current ensures you receive all communications from GST authorities regarding notice(s), assessment(s), updates etc.


### Consult Professionals When Needed


For complex matters like eligibility for ITC or interpretation of rules seek advice from chartered accountant or GST practitioner. Expert guidance will prove useful when handling GST authority notices, assessments or dispute resolution. Keep abreast of mid-year clarifications or notifications thru official website(s) or other reliable source(s). Being part of expert networks or keeping updated through official channels is a key aspect of maintaining compliance.


##


Summary: GST Return Filing in 2026


GST return filing in 2026 brings stricter enforcement, in addition to simplification. The three-year return filing limit, the auto-computation of late fees, and portal validations call for accuracy and punctuality. However, the two-tier taxing system, automated e-invoicing, and streamlined reconciliation procedures make it simpler for organized businesses.


It is in proactive strategies such as staying informed of changes in regulations, filing schedules, to name a few. It is important to realize that compliance goes beyond abiding by rules to avoid fines. It also enhances trust between partners in addition to avoiding interruptions due to regulations.

##


FAQs on GST Return Filing


#### What Is the GST Return Filing Process in 2026?


Businesses must file GSTR-1 for outward supplies and GSTR-3B for tax summaries via the GST portal. Reconciliation with GSTR-2B ensures eligible ITC before submission.


#### What Are GSTR-1, GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B?


GSTR-1 reports sales, GSTR-2B provides ITC details for reconciliation, and GSTR-3B summarizes net tax payable. Filing in sequence helps businesses reconcile the figures and correct errors.


#### What Documents Are Required to File a GST Return?


You need sales and purchase invoices, GSTIN, HSN/SAC codes, payment challans, and reconciled data from GSTR-2B. Businesses using Cashfree can streamline invoicing and record keeping.


#### What Are the GST Return Filing Due Dates?


Monthly GSTR-1 is due by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th. QRMP filers follow staggered GSTR-3B deadlines on the 22nd or 24th, based on the state of registration. Quarterly GSTR-1 is generally due on the 13th of the month after the quarter ends.


#### Can Businesses File GST Returns Offline?


No, GST returns are filed digitally through the GST portal or an approved channel. However, data can be prepared offline and uploaded using Excel-based utilities provided on the portal.


#### How Do I File a Nil GST Return Online?


Open **Returns Dashboard** , select the tax period and choose the relevant return. If you meet the nil filing conditions, select the nil option, preview the return and file it with DSC or EVC.
